title: Rapid yeast-based screen for Functionally Relevant Amino Acids (RS-FRAA) in a protein
protocol: Perform two PCR reactions in parallel using the uncut plasmid harboring your GOI as template.
Use the sense flanking primer and antisense mutagenesis primer for one reaction (PCR-1a).
For the second reaction, use the antisense flanking primer and sense mutagenesis primer (PCR-1b).
Validate successful PCR amplification via DNA gel electrophoresis.
Troubleshoot if PCR reaction (PCR-1a or PCR-1b) leads to no amplification or products of different sizes.
For fusion PCR reaction, PCR-2, use the flanking primer pair and as template add 1/10th – 1/100th of the reaction volume of each of the two PCR reactions (PCR-1a and PCR-1b).
Validate successful PCR amplification via DNA gel electrophoresis.
Conduct PCR-2 using your GOI as the template.
Perform PCR-3.
Validate successful PCR amplification via DNA gel electrophoresis.
Do not discard the amplicon from PCR-3 (PCR-3 amplicon).
Pause point: Completed PCR reactions can be kept frozen without any time limit.
Streak out yeast on solid YPD medium to obtain single colonies if vector or plasmid is not available (day -2 or -3, 10 min).
Inoculate liquid medium with yeast to generate a fresh overnight culture the day before (day -1, 15–30 min).
Cut plasmid and test for complete digestion (day 0, 4–5 hrs including waiting times).
Make plasmid dilutions (day 0, 10 min).
Transform plasmid dilutions into yeast (day +1, the whole day including waiting times).
Evaluate numbers of transformants (day +3 or +4, 15 min).
Cut plasmid with restriction enzymes using 5 μg of plasmid DNA in a 200 μL reaction volume.
Perform DNA gel electrophoresis to validate the complete restriction digest.
In parallel, perform single digest reactions for each enzyme.
Use samples A – D from the restriction digests for validation via DNA electrophoresis.
Store the remaining sample A at −20°C or −80°C if the digestion was complete.
Cut the chosen vector at the multiple cloning sites using the restriction enzyme identified.
Validate the restriction digest via DNA electrophoresis using 20 μL of each sample.
Store the remaining sample A at −20°C or −80°C if the digest was complete.
Determine the appropriate working concentration for the linearized plasmid.
Dilute the linearized plasmid 10, 20, 40, and 80-fold in double deionized sterile water.
Generate competent yeast cells.
Grow yeast overnight in a glass tube with cap at 30°C using the test tube rotator.
Transfer 1 mL of overnight culture to each of two sterile 250 mL flasks containing 50 mL of YPD medium.
Grow cultures at 30°C, shaking at 160 rpm until OD600 reaches 0.8 but not higher than 1 (takes approximately 3 hours).
Transfer each culture into a sterile 50 mL Falcon tube aseptically.
Centrifuge the cultures at 1,500–2,000 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant.
Resuspend each pellet in 8 mL Solution I.
Incubate for 30 minutes shaking at 30°C for same day transformations.
Or incubate at 4°C (not shaking) until the next day.
Centrifuge cells at 1,500–2,000 × g (4,000 rpm for MultifugeX1R Pro) for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend each pellet in 500 μL of solution I.
Combine the content of the two Falcon tubes into one tube.
Keep at 4°C until usage (same or next day).
Transform the plasmid dilutions into yeast.
In parallel, transform 1 μL of uncut plasmid as a positive control.
Also in parallel, transform no plasmid DNA to serve as a negative control.
Heat an aliquot of herring sperm DNA for 10 minutes at 100°C.
Quickly cool the heated DNA at 4°C.
Aliquot 5 μL of herring sperm DNA into each tube.
Add circular plasmid and dilutions of linearized plasmid to respective tubes according to the table.
Resuspend competent cells by pipetting up and down slowly.
Add 100 μL of competent cells to each tube.
Mix samples by pipetting up and down slowly.
Incubate for 30 min at 30°C.
Add 700 μL of Solution II (40% PEG-Li-Acetate solution) to each tube.
Mix the sample well.
Incubate for 45 min at 30°C, shaking.
Subject to heat shock treatment at 42°C for 15 min.
Transfer samples to ice for 2–5 min.
Pellet cells at ∼100 × g (1,000 rpm for Pico centrifuge) for 3 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Repeat the centrifugation for 1 min.
Take off the remainder of the supernatant using a 20-100 μL pipette.
Add 10–20 sterile glass beads to each plate containing media that selects for transformants.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 50–100 μL of SD liquid medium lacking supplements and lacking a carbon source.
Transfer each sample to a plate containing the appropriate selective medium and the glass beads.
Shake plates back and forth to make the beads move around on the solid medium.
Tip off the glass beads into a container with 70% ethanol solution.
Incubate plates at 30°C for 2–3 days.
Determine the number of transformants obtained for each plasmid dilution.
Determine which linearized plasmid dilution leads to no more than 5–10 transformants.
Generate circularized plasmid containing the GOI with a desired point mutation.
Prepare fresh liquid yeast overnight culture the day before transformation.
Perform yeast transformation on the day of preparation.
Wait for 2–3 days after transformation.
Select transformants on day +2 or +3 post-transformation.
Retrieve and store selected mutant transformants on day +3 or +4.
Conduct colony PCR on day +3, +4, or +5 to confirm mutations.
Inoculate a single yeast colony in YPD medium.
Grow overnight at 30°C using a test tube rotator for 20–40 hours.
Transfer 1 mL of the overnight culture to a sterile 250 mL flask containing 50 mL of YPD medium.
Grow at 30°C, shaking at 160 rpm until OD600 reaches 0.8 but not higher than 1.
Transfer the culture into a sterile 50 mL Falcon tube aseptically.
Centrifuge at 1,500–2,000 × g for 5 minutes and discard supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 8 mL Solution I (0.1 M Li-Acetate solution).
Incubate for 30 minutes shaking at 30°C for same day transformations or incubate at 4°C until the next day.
Pellet cells by centrifuging at 1,500–2,000 × g (4,000 rpm for MultifugeX1R Pro, Thermo Fisher Scientific) for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 500 μL of solution I.
Keep resuspended cells at 4°C until usage (same or next day).
Heat an aliquot of herring sperm DNA for 10 min at 100°C.
Quickly cool the heated herring sperm DNA at 4°C.
Lay out aseptically sterile 1.5 mL microfuge tubes, one tube for each sample.
Aliquot 5 μL of herring sperm DNA into each tube.
Add 5 μL of linearized plasmid DNA, PCR-3 amplicon, and uncut plasmid to the respective tubes.
Resuspend competent cells by slowly pipetting up and down.
Add 100 μL of competent cells to each tube containing DNA.
Mix thoroughly by slowly pipetting up and down.
Incubate for 30 min at 30°C.
Add 700 μL of Solution II (40% PEG-Li-Acetate solution) to the tubes.
Mix well by pipetting into the bottom of the tube, closing it, and shaking vigorously horizontally.
Incubate for 45 min at 30°C while shaking.
Subject samples to heat shock treatment at 42°C for 15 min.
Transfer samples to ice for 2–5 min.
Store samples for up to 20 hours at 4°C.
Pellet cells at approximately 100 × g (1,000 rpm for Pico centrifuge) for 3 minutes and discard the supernatant.
Repeat the centrifugation for 1 minute.
Remove the remaining supernatant using a pipette between 20–200 μL.
Add 10–20 sterile glass beads (diameter 3–5 mm) to each plate containing media that selects for transformants.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 50–100 μL of SD medium lacking supplements and carbon source.
Transfer each sample to a plate containing appropriate selective medium along with the glass beads.
Shake plates back and forth to spread cells on the plate using moving beads.
Tip off the glass beads into a container with 70% ethanol solution (the beads can be reused).
Incubate plates at 30°C for 2–3 days.
Determine the number of transformants of the linearized plasmid-alone control.
Pick single colonies using sterile toothpicks and patch them on a fresh plate.
Incubate the patched plate for 1 day.
Use a sterile toothpick to transfer cells from the plate into a sterile cryogenic tube containing 30% glycerol for storage at -80°C.
Aseptically transfer a tiny amount of yeast cells (barely visible with the naked eye) from the plate using the tip of a sterile yellow pipette tip into a PCR reaction mix.
Design primers that anneal to DNA flanking the area of recombination to yield a PCR amplicon preferably 200-400 bp long for colony PCR.
Grow yeast cells freshly, do not use stored plates from the fridge.
Ensure the tip’s tip is submerged in the PCR reaction mix while rolling it back and forth against the tube wall to transfer cells into liquid.
Place samples into the PCR cycler and start the machine.
Perform initial denaturation at 95°C for 5 minutes followed by PCR cycles according to manufacturer's instructions.
Prepare master plates on day -1.
Replica plate on day 0.
Select diploid strains on day +2 or +3.
Retrieve diploid strains on days +3 or +4.
Store diploid strains on day +4 or +5.
Prepare master plate in liquid medium from day -1 to -3.
Prepare overnight culture of mating strain on day -1.
Set up mating on day 0.
Select for diploid strains on day +1 or +2.
Retrieve diploid strains on days +3 or +4.
Store diploid strains on day +4 or +5.
Draw a grid on the back of a plate containing appropriate selective medium to maintain the plasmid in mutation transformants.
Patch the mutation transformants on the plate minding the borders given by the grid.
Include a transformant harboring the unmutated plasmid.
Incubate plate-1 and plate-2 upside-down for 15–20 hours at 30°C.
Ensure the cells have just grown up without being overgrown.
Mount a sterile velvet onto the replica plater under sterile conditions.
Secure the velvet cloth using the supplied ring.
Transfer cells from plate-1 onto the velvet.
Transfer cells from plate-2 onto the same velvet so that patches intersect with those from plate 1.
Transfer cells from the velvet onto fresh plates.
Incubate replica plates at 30°C for 2–3 days.
Take cells from the middle of the grown patch of diploid cells using a sterile toothpick.
Transfer each cell to a sterile glass tube containing liquid medium that selects for diploids.
Grow cultures until saturation at 30°C, agitating.
Aseptically transfer a drop (about 5 μL) from each culture to solid medium selecting for diploids.
Let the drop dry in and incubate overnight upside-down at 30°C.
Store the master plate at 4°C.
Use a sterile toothpick to transfer cells directly from the plate into a sterile cryogenic tube containing 30% glycerol, vortex, and then transfer to -80°C for permanent storage.
Commence phenotypic screening using saturated liquid cultures within 1-2 days.
In a 96 flat-well microtiter plate, add 180 μL of SD liquid medium suitable for maintaining the plasmid present in mutation transformants to all wells.
Inoculate wells B2-11, C2-11, D3-11, E3-11, F2-11 with mutation transformants.
Inoculate wells G2-6 with transformants that only serve as a control for mating.
Cover the microtiter plate-1 with its lid.
Place plate-1 into a zip lock bag containing a few holes to allow air exchange.
Incubate plate-1 at 30°C until the bottom of the wells is covered with cells, which takes 1–3 days depending on how many cells were used for inoculation.
Inoculate a sterile glass tube containing 4 ml of YPD medium with a colony of the mating strain and grow it for 15–20 hours at 30°C using a test tube rotator.
Mix 10 μL of the mating strains’ fresh overnight culture with the wells B2-11, C2-11, D3-11, E3-11, F2-11, and G9-11 on plate-2.
Pipette up and down the content of the wells in column 2 of plate-1 to resuspend the cells.
Transfer 10 μL from the wells in column 2 of plate-1 to the corresponding wells in column 2 of plate-2.
Repeat the process for each well, transferring 10 μL using new tips each time for wells 3–11 on plate-2.
Cover plate-2 with its lid.
Place plate-2 in a zip-lock bag with holes and incubate at 30°C until cells have covered the bottom of the well.
In a fresh 96 flat-well microtiter plate, add 180 μL of liquid medium suitable for selecting for diploids.
Transfer 10 μL from each well in plate-2 to its respective well in plate-3.
Cover the plate with its lid.
Incubate plate-3 in a zip-lock bag with holes at 30°C until visible growth is seen, which takes 1–3 days.
Note: Only diploid cells will be able to grow, while the wells containing haploid cells should remain clear.
If a master plate for future experiments is needed, transfer a drop (about 5 μL) onto solid medium selecting for diploids.
Let the drop dry in and incubate overnight (15–20 h) upside-down at 30°C.
Use directly or store at 4°C.
Note: Diploid cells do not stay viable for a long time. It is highly recommended to use some of these cells for permanent storage at −80°C.
Use a sterile toothpick to transfer cells directly from the plate into a sterile cryogenic tube containing 30% glycerol.
Vortex the mixture.
Transfer the mixture to -80°C for storage.
Prepare fresh overnight cultures of yeast transformants.
Set up growth assay using overnight cultures.
Monitor growth over weeks 1 to 2 or longer, depending on phenotypic changes.
Inoculate sterile glass tubes containing 4 mL of appropriate liquid medium with a colony of the respective strain.
Grow cultures for 39–48 hours at the appropriate conditions.
Incubate cultures at 30°C using the test tube rotator.
Check the OD600nm of the cultures after 33-42 hours of incubation.
Check the OD600nm again 6-12 hours later.
Continue growing the cultures until there is no change in OD600nm.
Inoculate strains for the same growth assay into separate sterile glass tubes containing the same batch of liquid medium.
Ensure similar starting densities and the same time period under the same conditions (e.g., temperature) for inoculated strains.
Add 180 μL of SD medium lacking glucose as a carbon source and lacking supplements to wells in columns 2–5 of a microtiter plate.
Align the two middle tips of the multichannel pipette with the respective intersections of the grid on the petri plate.
Slowly move closer to the agar surface and align the outer tips with their respective intersections of the grid.
Press the button of the pipette until the resistance point when the tips are 1–2 mm close to the surface, so that the content hangs on the tips.
Release any residual content from the tips once the drops touch the agar surface.
Conduct 10-fold serial dilutions using an 8-channel pipette set to 20 μL.
Mix the contents of the wells in column 1.
Transfer 20 μL from column 1 to column 2.
Pipet up and down several times the content of the wells in column 2.
Transfer 20 μL from column 2 to column 3.
Repeat the process, transferring cells from column 3 to column 4.
Transfer cells from column 4 to column 5.
Place the lid on the microtiter plate to keep the samples sterile.
Select petri plates containing solid medium for scoring phenotypic effects.
Prepare control plates with solid medium that do not elicit phenotypic effects.
Add a grid to the back of each plate as a guide when transferring 5 μL of each dilution from the microtiter plates.
Using an 8-channel pipette set to 50 μL, pipet up and down the cells in the microtiter plate.
Resuspend cells in the highest dilution (column 5).
Transfer 5 μL from column 5 to each plate using an 8-channel pipette.
Repeat the process for microtiter plate columns in descending order: 4, 3, 2, and finally 1.
Align the middle tips of the 8-channel pipette with the respective intersections of the grid (Figure 6F, pink arrows and dotted lines) to avoid puncturing the medium surface.

If available, use a frogger or pin-replicator instead of an 8-channel pipette for transferring cells from microtiter plates to agar plates. Determine the volume transferred by each pin, typically around 1 μL.
Let the samples fully dry in.
Incubate plates at 30°C, up-side-down.
Place the plates into a bag with small holes for long-term growth experiments.
Add a wet paper towel inside the bag for long-term growth experiments.
Monitor the growth until all the highest dilutions have generated colonies of at least 1 mm diameter.
Place the plates right-side up on the scanner for documentation.
Take off the lids before scanning the plates.
Scan the plates using a document scanner.
Place the lids back on the plates after scanning.
Return the experiment to 30°C immediately after scanning.
Quantify the amount of growth for each strain by eye.
Convert the observed growth into numerical values.
Calculate growth rates for each strain.
Plot the calculated growth rates in a bar graph.
Assign growth scores for each strain on the growth-assay plate.
Determine the overall growth score for the control plates.
Divide the overall growth score from the growth-assay plate by that of the control plate to obtain the adjusted growth score for each individual strain.
Divide the adjusted growth score of each strain by that of the reference strain to determine the relative growth rate.
Subject at least two independent mutation transformants to semi-quantitative growth assays.
Determine standard errors from the results for error bar representation in bar graphs.
Employ a student t-test to assess whether the mutated gene of interest significantly alters the growth rate compared to the control strain.
